subject.title: fix(sqlite): allow verified shared wal backports

question: Should OpenClaw support an operator-asserted environment-variable bypass for the SQLite WAL-corruption guard when a distribution claims a backport, or retain the existing version-based fail-closed policy?
rationale: The code cannot portably establish that an arbitrary shared SQLite 3.46.1 package contains the required upstream fix, so accepting a user assertion changes the product's data-integrity safety boundary rather than completing a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Retain the fail-closed guard
options.body: Reject shared SQLite versions outside the known-safe release lines until a distributable, verifiable compatibility mechanism exists.

options.title: Approve a supported override contract
options.body: Document exactly who verifies a distro backport, how operators record that evidence, how the override is scoped, and add real-image proof before accepting the bypass.

recommendation.title: Retain the fail-closed guard
recommendation.body: Reject shared SQLite versions outside the known-safe release lines until a distributable, verifiable compatibility mechanism exists.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked regression traces the relevant SQLite safety enforcement to vincentkoc's adjacent safety work.
